observations.title: What If Earth Stopped Spinning?
observations.desc:
What If Earth Stopped Spinning?

If the ground stopped and the air did not, the air at the equator would keep going at more than 1,500 km/h, faster than sound.

Sources: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (highest gust 408 km/h, Barrow Island, 10 April 1996). Equatorial rotation about 1,670 km/h. Speed of sound at sea level about 1,235 km/h.
https://wmo.asu.edu/content/world-highest-wind-gust-recorded-cyclone

Pictures: NASA EPIC imagery. Facts: every number is checked against the source above.
Image credits: NASA.

observations.title: How Thin Are Saturn's Rings?
observations.desc:
How Long Do Saturn's Rings Have Left?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55AEQwvs36g

Saturn's main rings span tens of thousands of kilometres across, yet in places they are only about ten metres thick — ten times thinner than a 100-metre playing field. Drop through those ten metres and you are in open space again.

Sources: NASA, Saturn Fact Sheet / Cassini Solstice Mission (main rings ~10 metres thick in places); Iess et al. 2019, Science (Cassini Grand Finale ring mass and structure).

Pictures: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute Cassini imagery (PIA18367, PIA21057, PIA09805, PIA06092, PIA08992, PIA07872, PIA21886) alongside AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute.

observations.title: How Close Will Asteroid Apophis Pass Earth on Friday the 13th?
observations.desc:
An Asteroid Will Skim Past Earth on Friday the 13th

Apophis, 340 metres wide, passes 32,000 kilometres up on 13 April 2029, inside the ring of satellites at about 36,000 kilometres. It will miss.

Sources: NASA, Apophis Facts (340 m wide; 32,000 km from the surface on 13 April 2029; geosynchronous satellites about 36,000 km up; no impact risk for at least 100 years).
https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/apophis-facts/

Pictures: AI-generated scenes alongside NASA imagery. Facts: every number is checked against the source above.
Image credits: NASA.

Watch the full film: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VBaYRPp85Sw
